summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with embedded software experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Skilled in C and C++, bare-metal firmware, FreeRTOS task coordination, and low-level UART and I2C driver development for camera and sensor bring-up, carried from requirements and architecture through integration testing and hardware verification.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national competitions and ran 10+ technical workshops on Arduino and PCB design, mentoring junior members on embedded fundamentals.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline for microscopic crack analysis using custom image stitching, a wavelet denoising bank (PSNR 86), and monocular depth estimation at ±8% error.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1), with a hand-written I2C driver and timer-triggered ADC scans on interrupt-driven capture.
Achieved a 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Architected a three-layer embedded system: a Flask-SocketIO edge server, an NVIDIA Jetson vision client, and an Arduino C++ motion controller linked over WebSocket and USB-serial.
Brought up dual VL53L0X ToF sensors through a TCA9548A I2C mux for a camera range-gate and 25 mm gripper trigger; ran TensorRT-optimized YOLO at 5.2× over eager PyTorch (56.7 → 10.9 ms).
Debugged 11 hardware and software integration failures including false-positive detections, servo brown-out, and stale frames; validated 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.
